title: Lesson 53 - Managing a Live Agent: Versions, Activation, and the Change Gate
description: Explain the process for managing and monitoring agents.

questions.question: A consultant must correct wording in an agent that is running in production without taking the live version out of service. What is the correct sequence?
options: Edit the live agent in place, then save, because saving updates the active version
Create a new version, edit and test it, commit it, then activate it, which deactivates the currently active version
Deactivate the agent, edit it, and reactivate it under the same version number
Commit the active version again with the fix, because recommitting overwrites the snapshot
questions.explanation: The change must go into a new version that is tested and committed before activation, and activating it retires the old active version automatically.

questions.question: What does committing an agent version do?
options: It publishes the version to every connected channel immediately
It merges the version into the active version's draft history
It deletes the previous version from Agentforce Builder
It saves a snapshot of the version to metadata and makes it available to activate, after which the version can no longer be edited
questions.explanation: Commit writes a frozen snapshot to metadata so the version can be activated, and the freeze is what stops you editing it afterward.

questions.question: Which statement about agent versions is correct?
options: Only one version of an agent can be active at a time, and activating a new version deactivates the prior active version
Multiple versions can be active at once so you can A/B test in production
A committed version can still be edited until it is activated
A draft version can be activated before it is committed
questions.explanation: The platform allows a single active version, so activating a new one automatically retires the old one.
